fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"The Water Tower That Survived","body":"The sharpest objection here is architectural. If the 1871 fire was a bombing run meant to erase old world buildings, why does so much grand stone still stand? William W. Boyington's Water Tower, finished in 1869 out of Joliet limestone, came through in full glory while its neighbors fell, and Oscar Wilde disliked it enough to call it a castellated monstrosity with pepper boxes stuck all over it in 1882. Old St. Patrick's from 1856, the Henry B. Clarke House from 1836, and Holy Family all survived. The Sherman House was rebuilt bigger, and the fire took only about a third of the city."},{"title":"A City Framed In Pine","body":"Chicago invented the building method that fed the fire. George Washington Snow framed a warehouse without hand cut joints in 1832, and a couple of years later the carpenter Augustine Taylor nailed St. Mary's Church together from light 2x4s for about $400, a technique mocked as balloon construction until it became known instead as Chicago construction. Its wall cavities ran from foundation to roof with no fire stops. Add roughly 60,000 buildings that were about 90 percent wood, 561 miles of raised plank sidewalk, 57 miles of tar coated wood block street, and one inch of rain from July to October."},{"title":"Nobody Left To Fight It","body":"The fire department was already broken before the first alarm sounded. In the six days before October 8, Chicago's roughly 185 to 219 firemen answered 27 alarms and worked 24 fires, then spent 14 to 17 hours on the Saturday night Red Flash fire that leveled four blocks of lumber yards and mills and cost a million dollars. Hook and Ladder Company 1 lost all of its apparatus, two steam engines were disabled, and Engine Company 6 reached the O'Leary barn after 22 hours of work and one hour of rest. Watchman Matthias Schaefer then misjudged the location by a mile, and the telegraph operator refused to correct the box."},{"title":"Rubble Without Bombs","body":"The Tartaria case leans on how much the ruins resemble Dresden after Allied incendiary bombing, and Chance grants the resemblance before explaining it. Nineteenth century mortar most likely lost its integrity somewhere around 600 to 800 degrees, while a fuel rich structural fire easily reaches 1,200, 1,400, even 2,000, so unbound brick simply collapsed into chaotic piles. Local Lemont limestone heated past 1,500 degrees becomes quicklime and crumbles to powder. The blurry roof edges offered as proof of hidden airships are halation, a known glass plate effect. Even the Tribune's fireproof 1869 headquarters burned, undone by paper, archives, and linseed oil ink."},{"title":"Who Cashed In Fastest","body":"The city's own 11th annual Board of Public Works report from July 1872 tallies about $200 million lost across 1,687 acres, names no cause, and the cause has stayed undetermined ever since. What followed is documented. Three days after the fire, Mayor Roswell Mason handed authority to Lieutenant General Philip Sheridan under effective martial law that guarded bank rubble instead of feeding anyone. Two days later he routed every relief dollar, five to ten million of it, to the private Chicago Relief and Aid Society, which closed its books with $600,000 unspent. Within 30 days Joseph Medill won the mayoralty by 46 points."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tartaria theory says the Great Chicago Fire of 1871 was firebombed to erase the Old World. Is this alternative history conspiracy possible?
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: The ruins from the great fire really do resemble a bombed out city. Could the brick and limestone buildings of Old Chicago collapse to rubble from an ordinary fire? Were the streets and sidewalks themselves burning? Why couldn't the firemen stop the blaze? And why is the official cause undetermined, 150 years later? My investigation looks at Chicago's construction methods, the amount of wood in the city, weather conditions of the time, "fireproof" buildings, surviving "Old World" architecture, martial law, and the consolidation of power by the city's industrial elites in the wake of the conflagration.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Grand Fire Trine Overhead", "body": "The sky over October 8th, 1871 held something an astrologer almost never gets to point at. The Moon at eleven degrees Leo trined Mars at eight degrees Sagittarius, Mars trined Chiron at eight degrees Aries, and Chiron trined back to the Moon, closing a genuine grand fire trine well inside the three degree orb that counts as tight. Mars carries fire, accidents and destruction. The waning crescent Moon carries dryness, barrenness and the burning off of dead wood. Chiron carries sudden wounds and structural flaws. Two of the three sat at the eighth degree, read as Scorpio's death and rebirth, while the Moon's eleventh degree read as Aquarian sudden disruption."}, {"title": "The Hidden Half Hour", "body": "Two charts get cast, one for the 8:30 PM ignition and one for the 9:00 PM citywide alarm, and the thirty minutes between them tell different stories. At 8:30 Pluto sat in the twelfth house of concealed motives, secret enemies and everything outside ordinary awareness, in Taurus, money and wealth, and square the Midheaven, the most public point of the chart. Neptune, all fog and false story, sextiled that same Midheaven, which reads as a cause that never gets satisfactorily settled, right down to Mrs. O'Leary's cow. By 9:00 the north node had crossed the ascendant in Gemini, the sign of communication, alarm and rumor."}, {"title": "The Facade In The Fourth House", "body": "Beneath the fire trine sits the fourth house, the foundations and roots of the chart, crowded with the Sun, Mercury and a retrograde Venus in fall in Virgo, which reads as a beautiful facade concealing dangerous imperfections in the way a city was built. Because Mercury rules the Gemini ascendant and answers to Venus, most of the chart ends up reporting to that one flawed placement. Laid against Chicago's incorporation chart of March 4th, 1837, the fire's Moon in Leo lands within one degree of the city's own Mars and Jupiter conjunction, and the fire's Pluto opposes the city's Saturn, its structure and order."}, {"title": "The Night The Middle Of The Country Burned", "body": "Chicago was not alone that night. Peshtigo, Wisconsin lost over a million acres and sixteen towns, with a death toll estimated between 1,200 and 2,500 people, by a wide margin the deadliest fire in American history. Across Green Bay, a fire that began south of New Franken ran with the wind through Union, Brussels, Forestville and Williamsville, leaving 7,500 people homeless. The Great Michigan Fire was at least three fires burning at once, destroying Holland and Manistee, damaging Port Huron and Alpena, taking ninety percent of the homes in the Thumb, and killing loggers scattered through woods that nobody had a list for."}, {"title": "Donnelly's Comet And Its Heirs", "body": "The comet reading traces back to Ignatius Donnelly, a Minnesota congressman whose 1882 book Atlantis: The Antediluvian World argued that Plato's account was literally true, and whose 1883 follow up, Ragnarok: The Age of Fire and Gravel, blamed a prehistoric comet and reached for Chicago and Peshtigo as modern proof. The timing kills it. Biela's comet split in two in 1846, disappeared, and left behind the Andromedids, which peak in late November, and the spectacular 1872 Andromedid storm set nothing alight. Donnelly's frame still runs through Blavatsky, Steiner, Churchward, Cayce, Hancock, the Electric Universe crowd, and finally Tartaria and its mud flood."}]

It's just a document where they're counting the beans about what they lost.","author":"Chance Garton","portrait":"https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"},{"text":"The exterior walls are basically like chimneys with houses in the middle.","author":"Chance Garton","portrait":"https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"},{"text":"If the fire was some kind of clandestine operation to erase all the evidence of the old world architecture in Chicago, why would so much of that architecture remain standing?","author":"Chance Garton","portrait":"https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"},{"text":"The historical record shows the exact opposite.
